🏛️ Big one, and it has barely been reported properly.

English mayors are about to start keeping a share of the tax raised in your area instead of getting a grant from Whitehall.

📅 April 2027 — mayors keep more of local business rates
📅 April 2028 — mayors get a slice of local income tax receipts
📅 28 October — the detail lands in John Healey's first Budget

To be fair: income tax RATES are not changing. This is a share of receipts, not a power to put your tax up. I am not going to pretend otherwise.

But here is what worries me 👇
⚠️ Local scrutiny of mayors is the weakest part of the whole mayoral model, and nothing robust has been built to replace Whitehall oversight
⚠️ Tax receipts are volatile in a way grants are not — and poorer areas carry that risk
⚠️ Turnout at the last Greater Manchester mayoral by-election was 25%

Power closer to home? Yes. I have argued for that in Lancashire for years. But build the accountability FIRST.
